title: Judging LLMs: Alex Volkov
talk_summary: A theatrical, vendor-sponsored talk (Weights & Biases) that uses mock court cases to argue three practical points: trace/log everything in production, iterate on prompts before fine-tuning, and use a layered eval strategy (programmatic assertions, human-in-the-loop, LLM-as-judge) with custom criteria and validated judges. The concrete mechanisms are the three eval types and the warning that LLM judges need bias checks and human oversight.

takeaways.technique: Layered eval stack: programmatic + human + LLM-judge
takeaways.what_they_do: Combine three scoring methods: programmatic assertions (unit-test-like checks for format/numerical/code output), human-in-the-loop review during development, and LLM-as-judge for cheap scale on open-ended outputs.

takeaways.technique: Custom criteria instead of off-the-shelf rubrics
takeaways.what_they_do: Define eval criteria specific to the application rather than using generic/default rubrics; the speaker shows per-app criteria like contrast, relevance, polish for an HTML generator.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the offthe-Shelf criteria are not that great you have to create your custom ones ... for your own business

takeaways.technique: Validate the validator (bias-check the LLM judge)
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat the LLM judge as fallible: check it for biases, iterate its system prompt and examples, and keep humans in the loop; the talk itself demonstrates a judge being prompt-injected mid-demo.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's important to check your judges also for biases ... remember to validate your validators

takeaways.technique: Trace and log every LLM call with inputs/outputs/params
takeaways.what_they_do: Instrument all LLM calls (prompts, params, inputs/outputs, call hierarchy for agents/RAG) so regressions are debuggable and eval datasets can be built from real production examples.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you put anything of value in production you have to trace and log everything

takeaways.technique: Iterate prompts before fine-tuning / escalating model cost
takeaways.what_they_do: Exhaust prompt iteration (chain-of-thought, flow engineering, multi-agent mixtures) before spending on fine-tuning or heavier models.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have to iterate on prompts before you find tune ... you can get very very far with methods like a Chain of Thought prompting
takeaways.numbers: 6% benchmark improvement cited for premature fine-tuning case (illustrative)
